default.prompt:
Create a deterministic hand-authored 32×32 pixel top-down cottage tileset. Output one 128×96 image arranged as a 4-column × 3-row grid with no margin or spacing. Read frames left-to-right, then top-to-bottom. Draw exactly these nine tiles in this exact order:
Frame 0 — Stone floor: seamless gray square flagstones with subtle grout and wear; walkable.
Frame 1 — Wood floor: seamless warm-brown horizontal floorboards with restrained grain; walkable.
Frame 2 — Plaster wall: a straight horizontal pale-plaster wall segment with dark timber trim, connecting cleanly at the left and right cell edges; blocked.
Frame 3 — Timber wall: a straight horizontal cottage wall segment with exposed dark beams and pale infill, connecting cleanly at the left and right cell edges; blocked.
Frame 4 — Rug: a centered red cottage rug with gold bands over a floor base; walkable decoration.
Frame 5 — Hearth: a centered stone-and-timber fireplace with a warm flame over a floor base; blocked furniture.
Frame 6 — Table: a centered round wooden table viewed from above over a wood-floor base; blocked furniture.
Frame 7 — Bed: a centered single wooden bed with pale bedding and a blue pillow over a wood-floor base; blocked furniture.
Frame 8 — Wall corner: one 90-degree L-shaped plaster-and-timber wall corner whose arms exit through the top and right cell edges, matching the thickness, palette, and connectors of frames 2 and 3; blocked and designed to be rotated in quarter turns.
Leave row 3 columns 2–4 fully transparent because they are outside the nine-tile count. Use one consistent palette, orthographic top-down perspective, and crisp pixel edges. Keep every tile isolated within its 32×32 cell. Do not add text, labels, borders, padding, extra tiles, or reorder any frame.
